Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Her element — cadmium: a soft, bluish-silver metal, zinc's younger sibling in the table, found in 1817 by a German inspector of pharmacies who wondered why a white zinc powder turned yellow when heated, and named from cadmia, an old word for zinc ore that honours Cadmus, founder of Thebes; with sulphur it becomes the blazing cadmium yellow painters love, with selenium the deep cadmium red; behind those sunny colours hides a poison that softens bones; it also swallows neutrons in reactors, and as tiny crystals it glows any colour from yellow to red according to their size alone — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.
